entities.summary:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO), established in 1950, serves as a specialized agency of the United Nations dedicated to meteorology, climatology, hydrology, and related fields. Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, it plays a critical role in coordinating global efforts to monitor and understand weather, climate, and water resources, impacting millions of lives worldwide. The WMO's establishment was influenced by the increasing recognition of the need for international cooperation in weather forecasting and climate research in the post-World War II era, as nations sought to rebuild and address environmental challenges.

The WMO operates a network of meteorological and hydrological services, facilitating the exchange of data and research among member countries. Notably, it developed the Global Framework for Climate Services (GFCS) in 2012 to enhance climate data availability and usability, which is vital for disaster risk reduction and sustainable development. The organization also plays a crucial role in the World Weather Watch, a comprehensive program aimed at monitoring and predicting weather phenomena globally, thereby improving weather prediction accuracy and response strategies in the face of natural disasters.

The legacy of the WMO is profound, as it has laid the groundwork for enhanced international collaboration on climate issues, influencing policies and practices in numerous nations. Its work has led to improved understanding of climate change and its impacts, fostering initiatives aimed at mitigating adverse effects. As such, the WMO has inherited a pivotal role in shaping global climate change discussions and has become a cornerstone in the fight against environmental degradation and climate-related disasters.
